name: Peoples of the North American West
summary: The peoples of the Great Basin, the Plateau and the Pacific Northwest coast, from desert foragers to salmon-fishing nations whose totem poles and potlatch feasts are famous.
wikiTitle: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast
borderNames: North American Pacific foraging, hunting and fishing peoples

knownFor.label: Totem poles
knownFor.note: Carved cedar poles showing family histories and crests.

knownFor.label: Potlatch
knownFor.note: Feasts where hosts gave away goods to show status.

knownFor.label: Cedar plank houses
knownFor.note: Large houses of red cedar on the Northwest Coast.

location.value: Western North America: the Pacific Northwest coast, the Columbia Plateau and the Great Basin.
location.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast; Wikipedia: Great Basin tribes

terrain.value: Rainforest coasts, river valleys, plateaus and deserts.
terrain.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast; Wikipedia: Great Basin tribes

climate.value: Wet and mild on the coast; dry in the Great Basin.
climate.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast; Wikipedia: Great Basin tribes

resources.value: Salmon, cedar, shellfish, pine nuts, seeds.
resources.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast; Wikipedia: Great Basin tribes

disasters.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast; Wikipedia: Great Basin tribes

population.value: Unknown; the Northwest Coast was densely populated for foragers.
population.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast; Wikipedia: Great Basin tribes

urbanisation.value: Permanent villages on the coast; mobile camps in the Great Basin.
urbanisation.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast; Wikipedia: Great Basin tribes

disease.value: Smallpox, linked to Spanish expeditions in 1774, 1775 and 1779, may have killed as much as 90% of some local peoples.
disease.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast (checked 13 Nov 2026)

migration.value: Shifting groups over thousands of years.
migration.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast; Wikipedia: Great Basin tribes

economicBase.value: The Northwest Coast, from the Alaska Panhandle to Northern California, lived on cedar and salmon, caught by hook and line, nets, traps and spears.
economicBase.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast (checked 13 Nov 2026)

tradeRoutes.value: Trade along rivers; the Chinook Jargon trade language.
tradeRoutes.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast; Wikipedia: Great Basin tribes

wealth.value: Wealth in goods shown at potlatches on the coast.
wealth.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast; Wikipedia: Great Basin tribes

moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast; Wikipedia: Great Basin tribes

inequality.value: Ranked societies on the coast, with nobles, commoners and slaves.
inequality.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast; Wikipedia: Great Basin tribes

governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast; Wikipedia: Great Basin tribes

languageWriting.value: The Great Basin tribes (Shoshone, Ute, Mono, Northern Paiute) speak Numic languages; Pacific Northwest languages include Wakashan, Salishan, Chimakuan and Chinookan.
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Great Basin and Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast (checked 13 Nov 2026)

artsArchitecture.value: Totem poles, masks, woven Chilkat blankets, baskets.
artsArchitecture.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast; Wikipedia: Great Basin tribes

socialStructure.value: Potlatches marked events such as a new chief, marriages and a chief’s funeral; the coast was among the most densely populated Indigenous areas in Canada, with the Coast Salish in the tens of thousands before contact.
socialStructure.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast (checked 13 Nov 2026)

dailyLife.value: Cedar plank houses on the coast, pit houses on the Plateau, brush shelters in the Great Basin; salmon, roots, pine nuts.

neighbours.value: Plains and Southwest peoples, later Europeans.
neighbours.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast; Wikipedia: Great Basin tribes

ideasReligions.value: Christian missions; the potlatch was banned in Canada (1885–1951).
ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast; Wikipedia: Great Basin tribes

colonisation.value: Colonised by the US and Canada.
colonisation.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast; Wikipedia: Great Basin tribes

riseSignals.value: Great Basin: Paleo-Indians from as early as 10,000 BC, Desert Archaic people about 9,000 to 1,500 years ago, the Fremont about 1,500 to 700 years ago, then the Shoshone. The Plateau and Pacific Northwest are not covered on that page.
